meta.project: The High Horse Society Essay Judging Service

product_overview: The High Horse Society Essay Judging Service is a backend API service designed to enforce a higher standard of quality for essays submitted to the HHS social platform. It validates essays based on length, information density, and logical validity, ensuring only high-quality posts are accepted, supporting the vision of a healthier, more meaningful online interaction.
core_goals: Validate essays to ensure minimum quality standards: length, information density, logical validity.
Reject essays failing any validation criteria and approve those that pass all checks.
Support concurrent processing of multiple essay submissions.
Persist approved essays with versioning in a PostgreSQL database for retrieval and future contestation.
Provide API endpoints for submitting, judging, retrieving essays and health checks.
Implement optimistic concurrency control for version management in the database.
Facilitate a local development environment with a local PostgreSQL instance for full stack testing.
key_features: Health check endpoint (/health) to verify service availability.
Essay judging endpoint (/essay/judge) that accepts essays and returns validation results for length, density, and logical validity.
Essay submission endpoint (/essay/submit) for saving new essays or new versions to the database.
Essay retrieval endpoint (/essay/get) to fetch stored essays by latest or specific version.
Automatic rejection of essays less than 1000 words.
Information density validation using an LLM-assisted rubric.
Logical soundness validation using LLM analysis.
Storage of all essays along with quality metrics and version history in PostgreSQL.
Idempotency support through idempotency keys in essay submissions to prevent duplicate processing.
Concurrency handling to manage multiple requests simultaneously.
user_flow_summary: User submits an essay JSON to /essay/judge endpoint with idempotency_key, title, body, and optional sources and essay_id.
Service evaluates essay for length, density, and logical validity and returns a detailed JSON report indicating pass/fail status and rationale for each criterion.
If essay passes validation, user can submit the essay to /essay/submit endpoint to store it with versioning in the database.
User can retrieve stored essays via /essay/get endpoint, requesting either the latest version or a specific version by id.
Service health can be monitored via /health endpoint that returns service status.
validation_criteria: Service successfully rejects essays under 1000 words and returns appropriate rationale.
Information density and logical validity checks must produce boolean pass/fail with explanatory rationale.
Approved essays are stored with versioning data in PostgreSQL, and versions are managed with optimistic concurrency.
API endpoints must support expected request/response JSON formats as defined by OpenAPI schema.
Idempotency keys effectively prevent duplicate processing of identical essay submissions.
Local development environment must spin up PostgreSQL and full service stack on make dev command.
Service handles concurrent requests without failures or race conditions.
Database constraints enforce essay_id references or allow NULL as specified.

features.name: Essay Judging API
features.description: API to validate and judge essays based on length, information density, and logical validity. Includes health check endpoint.
